entries.oldTitle: has exactly one statement: a type-only `export type * from './types.ts'`
entries.newTitle: keeps `export type * from './types.ts'` as its first statement, so every Contract-stage type stays reachable unchanged
entries.note: P0-05's own later P-stage work renamed this it() block's title. C-stage's frozen observation (run 33562243795 @ 92174bb734) genuinely captured the old title passing at the time it greened -- predicate (iii) binds to that observation, not live-tree resolvability, so the C-stage cell's ACCEPTED status is unaffected. Recorded per BLOCKED-040.

entries.oldTitle: drops recomputable inputs from a completed, verified, pure step
entries.newTitle: drops recomputable inputs from a completed, verified step, whatever its effect class
entries.note: §12.46-A dropped `pure` from compaction's gate, leaving `completed && verified`. Purity could not be the gate: every step this DSL journals is an `agent()` call classed `side-effecting`, so a pure-only compaction was the identity function on every journal a real run can produce. The renamed cases assert the rule that now holds; the OLD titles' frozen observations genuinely captured the old rule passing when they greened, and predicate (iii) binds to that observation rather than to live-tree resolvability, so the affected cells' status is unchanged. Registered by the Executor with the measurement in BLOCKED-158.

retired.reason: Property changed, so a rename recorded a continuity that does not hold (§12.67, §12.68). §12.46-A removed compaction's unreachable `pure` gate and the guard became verification, so the old title and its replacement assert OPPOSITE guards — the P4-12.C.1 reading. Registering these as renames told verify-frozen-titles-resolvable the titles had merely moved, so it stopped looking and reported 0 UNRESOLVED for a day while three frozen titles had no live subject; the gap was found by counting `3 absent` in a signing report, not by a gate. Retired rather than deleted so the wrong call stays visible.
